{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises: are refunded orders included?
print("Total orders (including refunded):", len(df))
print("Refunded orders count:", (df['status'] == 'refunded').sum())

# Check if any rows have revenue = 999999.99 (QA orders)
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print("QA orders found:", len(qa_orders))

# Drop QA orders
df_clean = df[df['revenue'] != '999999.99'].copy()

# The contract says: population is ALL orders in the dataset
# So we must include refunded orders in the denominator for conversion rate
# Conversion rate = (converted = 1) / (all orders)
# But note: 'converted' is 1 only if the order completed checkout
# So the numerator is 'converted' == 1
# The denominator is the total number of orders in the dataset (all, including refunded)

# Compute conversion rate by channel using the full population (all orders, including refunded)
channel_conversion = df_clean.groupby('channel')['converted'].agg(['count', 'sum'])
channel_conversion['conversion_rate'] = channel_conversion['sum'] / channel_conversion['count']

# Compute the difference (email - paid_search)
overall_diff = channel_conversion.loc['email', 'conversion_rate'] - channel_conversion.loc['paid_search', 'conversion_rate']

# Print results
print("Conversion rates by channel (using full population of orders):")
print(channel_conversion[['conversion_rate']].round(4))
print("\nOverall difference (email - paid_search):", overall_diff)"}
